title: Private deploy acceptance and smoke validation playbook
author: Diego Marin
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines the minimum acceptance and smoke validation steps for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for SREs, deployment engineers, and customer success engineers who perform the final handoff and post-install verification. The goal is to provide a reproducible, time-boxed validation runbook that ensures the control plane, runtime, networking, security and observability are functioning to minimal SLAs before marking a deployment as ‘accepted’.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to: VPC-based private deployments and fully on-prem packages deployed by Redwood delivery teams or partner integrators.
- Not intended for: deep performance tuning or long-term capacity testing (see separate perf-suite docs).
- Timebox: full acceptance run should be completable in 3–8 hours depending on environment and scale.

Quick summary of gates (acceptance criteria):
1) Control plane API: POST /v1/models/list returns 200 and <= 500ms median response within acceptance window.
2) Runtime health: all runtime agents report healthy and KV cache warm success for at least 3 recent requests.
3) Networking: egress and ingress ACLs allow required ports; inter-pod latency < 2ms in same AZ and < 20ms cross-AZ (target).
4) Observability: telemetry pipeline ingestion within 60s, 99th percentile metric latency < 120s.
5) Security: KMS integration confirmed and test key can be used to encrypt/decrypt a sample token.

Pre-flight checklist (1 hour)
- Confirm inventory: list of hosts, instance types, network CIDRs, control-plane endpoints, cluster IDs.
- Credentials: deployment admin account, KMS access, mock-customer API key created for testing.
- Telemetry: Prometheus endpoint, tracing collector endpoint, log forwarding destination verified.
- Backups: snapshot/backups taken for relevant volumes before running tests.

Minimum hardware & software baseline (table)
(Use this as the initial acceptance baseline; larger deployments require updated baselines in the customer requirements doc.)

| Component | Minimum spec (single AZ small) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Control plane VM | 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM | Control plane services run on this host (API, auth, UI) |
| Runtime worker (per GPU node) | 8 vCPU, 64 GB RAM, 1xA10/RTX6000 or equivalent | Adequate for single-model small-load smoke tests |
| Storage | 200 GB SSD | OS + model artifacts cache |
| Network | 1 Gbps internal | Bandwidth affects throughput testing |

Network and firewall validation (required checks)
- Required ports and protocols:
  - TCP 443 (control plane API ingress)
  - TCP 1443 (agent to control-plane gRPC)
  - UDP/TCP 514/1514 (optional syslog/secure logging)
  - TCP 9090 (Prometheus, metrics read-only)
  - TCP 9411 (Zipkin/Jaeger collector)
- Firewall test procedure (3 steps):
  1. From a customer app host: curl -v https://<control-plane-host>/health should return HTTP 200.
  2. From each runtime host: nc -zv <control-plane-host> 1443 (expect success).
  3. From telemetry host: curl -sS http://<prometheus-host>:9090/-/healthy (expect 'Prometheus is Healthy').

Baseline performance expectations (smoke targets)
- Single-token generation (small model): median latency <= 150 ms, 95th <= 400 ms.
- 512-token generation (larger model): median per-token latency consistent with model profile; goal: first-token within 500 ms on warm cache.
- KV cache hit rate: after warm-up sequence, expect >= 70% prefix cache hit rate for synthetic replay prompts.

Acceptance test sequence (ordered, time-boxed)
1) Control plane health and auth (15–30min)
   - Verify API health:
     curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TEST_KEY}" https://<control-plane>/v1/health
     Expected: {"status":"ok","services":["api","auth","db"]} and HTTP 200.
   - Verify auth: create a short-lived token via POST /v1/admin/tokens and perform a sample model list call.

2) Runtime and model load (30–60min)
   - Deploy a canary model variant (small open model recommended).
   - Verify agent registration: on each runtime node run:
     sudo systemctl status redwood-agent
     Expected: active (running) and no crashes in last 5m.
   - Trigger model load via API and validate model-state:
     curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TEST_KEY}" -d '{"model":"canary-small","action":"load"}' https://<control-plane>/v1/models/manage
     Expected: 200 and status 'loaded' for all targeted agents.

3) Telemetry and tracing verification (15–30min)
   - Emit a trace via test client that calls model generate endpoint with tracing enabled; confirm trace shows through control-plane -> router -> runtime.
   - Confirm metrics appear in Prometheus within 60s. Use query: up{job=~"redwood.*"} and expect target count == deployed services.

4) Smoke generation test (30–60min)
   - Run the canonical smoke script (example below) from a client host that uses the test API key. Execute 3 phases: cold, warm, and concurrency.
   - Expected results: no 5xx errors, success rate >= 99%, median latency <= smoke targets above.

5) Security integrations (15–30min)
   - KMS: encrypt/decrypt roundtrip using the configured key.
   - Secrets: attempt a test rotation of a short-lived secret and validate runtime picks up rotated secret without restart (if configured).

6) Observability retention and alerts (15min)
   - Trigger a synthetic error and ensure alert rule fires to the configured PagerDuty/Slack channel.
   - Confirm log timestamps and trace IDs correlate across services.

Smoke script examples and CLI snippets
- Minimal smoke curl for generation (small model):

  curl -s -X POST https://<control-plane>/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TEST_KEY}" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"canary-small","input":"Hello world","max_tokens":32}' | jq .

  Expected minimal response: JSON containing "text" and a non-empty "request_id".

- Automated smoke runner (python pseudo):
  # ./scripts/smoke_runner.py --count 200 --concurrency 5 
  # Validations: status==200, latency distribution logged to /tmp/smoke-report.json

Prometheus queries to validate (examples)
- Control plane API availability:
  sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane",status=~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane"}[5m]))
  -> Expect >= 0.995 during acceptance run.
- Runtime agent health:
  count(up{job="redwood-agent"} == 1) == <expected-agent-count>
- Model load latency (histogram):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(model_load_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) < 10

Rollback and failure isolation criteria
- Immediate rollback triggers (stop acceptance and roll back to previous stable config):
  - >1% 5xx rate on control plane APIs for 10 consecutive minutes.
  - Any runtime node repeated crash-loop within 5 minutes after model load.
  - KMS failures preventing encryption/decryption for 5 consecutive test calls.
- Partial rollback actions:
  1. Remove canary model from routing and restore previous routing weights.
  2. Drain and restart affected runtime nodes (one at a time).
  3. If control plane is impacted, switch to read-only mode and fail traffic to dedicated fallback region (if configured).

Escalation and ownership
- Primary owner during acceptance: private-deploy delivery engineer (tagged on deployment ticket).
- Engineering on-call: redwood-eng-oncall@redwood.ai (pager duty).
- Security contact for KMS/SEV: security@example-redwood.ai (for encryption and secrets incidents).
- When to escalate to core runtime team: model load latency > 2x baseline and sustained for 15m.

Acceptance sign-off
- Required approvers: Delivery Engineer, SRE Approver, Customer Success Engineer.
- Sign-off checklist items (each must be checked in the ticket):
  - [ ] API health verified
  - [ ] Runtime agents healthy and model loaded
  - [ ] Smoke generation tests passed (attach /tmp/smoke-report.json)
  - [ ] Metrics ingested and alert verified
  - [ ] KMS/Secrets validated
  - [ ] Backups/snapshots confirmed

Appendix: common troubleshooting commands
- Check agent logs:
  journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 500 --no-pager
- Inspect model cache state (on runtime node):
  /opt/redwood/bin/modelctl status --model canary-small --json
- Force a cache warm for a prefix set:
  /opt/redwood/bin/cache-warm --model canary-small --prefix-file /tmp/prefixes.txt
